title: lscov
summary: Solve linear least-squares systems with observation covariance weighting.

gpu_support.notes: GPU-resident numeric inputs are gathered to host. Provider-native dense least-squares acceleration is deferred to the eval-loop GPU fast-path audit.

description: `lscov(A,B)` solves the linear least-squares system `A*x = B`. `lscov(A,B,V)` treats `V` as an observation covariance matrix, or as a vector of observation weights. `lscov(A,B,V,alg)` accepts `"chol"` and `"orth"` algorithm selectors.
behaviors: `A` must be a nonempty 2-D numeric design matrix. `B` must be a vector with one value per row of `A`, or a matrix with the same number of rows as `A`.
The primary output has shape `size(A,2) x size(B,2)` for matrix right-hand sides, and `size(A,2) x 1` for vector right-hand sides.

`V` may be omitted, empty, a scalar weight, a weight vector with one value per observation, or a dense square covariance matrix matching the observation count. Weights must be finite and nonnegative with at least one positive value.

The default `"chol"` algorithm uses Cholesky transformation for positive-definite covariance matrices when possible. Singular positive semidefinite covariance matrices fall back to the SVD-backed `"orth"` transformation.
Requested outputs follow MATLAB's `[x,stdx,mse,S]` form. `stdx` matches the coefficient shape, `mse` is a `1 x size(B,2)` row, and `S` is available only when `B` is a vector.
Real and complex dense `A`/`B` are supported. Sparse inputs and provider-native GPU solves are not implemented in this slice.

examples.output: x is approximately [1; 2] and mse is 0.
The high-weight third observation has more influence on x.

faqs.question: Does `lscov` add an intercept automatically?
faqs.answer: No. Include a column of ones in `A` when the model should include an intercept.

faqs.question: Does `lscov` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. The current implementation gathers GPU inputs and runs the dense weighted least-squares solve on the host.
